headline: Result Update

highlights: Important Data • APL Apollo Tubes Ltd (APAT) reported its strongest-ever quarter in Q2FY27, with record volumes, EBITDA and net profit, as a sharp rebound in APL Apollo-branded and roofing sales more than offset continued disruption in UAE operations, steel shortages in the domestic market and stalled exports amid high container freight rates.

Revenue rose 27% YoY (+25% QoQ) to ₹7,002crs, while brand-led pricing, a richer value-added mix and tighter cost control lifted EBITDA/ton to nearly ₹6,000. • Sales volume stood at a record 963k tons in Q2FY27 (+13% YoY, +29% QoQ), taking H1FY27 volume to 1,708k tons (+4% YoY).

APL Apollo brand volumes rose to ~775k tons (+19% YoY, +36% QoQ) and Roofing products to ~135k tons (+29% YoY, +48% QoQ), while SG Premium fell to ~27k tons as management de- prioritised low-margin volumes amid the steel shortage, and UAE stayed at ~26k tons (-55% YoY) with the plant running at only ~40% of normal levels.

Management remains confident of 15-20% growth in APL Apollo and roofing volumes. • Operating expenses increased 26% YoY and 24% QoQ to ₹6,424crs in Q2FY27, driven mainly by higher volumes and raw- material costs (₹5,899crs, +26% YoY).
valuation: Near-term, roofing (capacity ~700k tons a year) is targeted at ~175k tons in Q3FY27 versus 135k tons in Q2, and UAE capacity will rise to 0.5mn tons by March 2027 on two new mills (₹8,000–10,000/ton EBITDA, ~₹500crs potential) against a current run rate of ~100k tons a year.

Management’s FY27 targets of 15–20% growth in these two segments and EBITDA of ~₹2,200cr appear achievable given the H1FY27 run-rate, with Q3FY27 EBITDA/ton guided above ₹6,000 and capex largely behind it (~₹200cr in H2).

Our FY27E EBITDA of ₹2,101cr sits below this target, pointing to upside risk to estimates, and a recovery in UAE operations (0.5mn tons of capacity by March 2027 at ₹8,000–10,000/ton EBITDA) would be incremental.

Normalisation of the UAE, domestic steel availability and container freight is also seen as the key to FY27 EBITDA of ~₹2,400crs (versus the ~₹2,200crs base guidance) and a possible ~₹3,000crs in FY28.
